object_description: two-storey volume floating above a recessed glazed ground floor, perforated by two courtyards
geometry_property: basement plus ground and two upper floors
vertical slats binding the upper floors
regular uniform facade on all sides
design_condition: the elongated volume develops along the avenue detached from the neighbouring hall facades, its all-round recessed glazed plinth creating no front or back and integrating the building equally into the existing structures

positive: The simple and clear volume has a regular, uniform facade on all sides
The new building appears as a floating two-storey structure on a glazed ground floor
Vertical slats bind the two upper floors into a single unit and the volume appears calm and natural
The all-round recessed plinth creates no explicit front and back and integrates the building equally into the existing structures
The building is integrated into the existing road network
The cascading main staircase provides access to all floors and creates places for informal encounters
The uses are arranged in an all-round, uncluttered layer along the facade
Two inner courtyards perforate the upper volume so inner areas are naturally lit and ventilated
The spatial programme is organised on a regular grid
The filter-like facade reduces views from outside, shades the facade behind and creates intimacy
The courtyards can contribute as extended open space in direct relation to the workspaces
Strengthening the avenues is welcomed as an important contribution to the discussion
The library is well and generously accommodated
Separate external use of hall, gymnastics room and lecture hall is possible
The designers give the building an unagitated independence and serenity among the large-scale sports buildings
negative: The circumferential visitors gallery is not required, prevents playing on the walls and is interrupted by the escape stairs
The public access offered by the gallery is perceived as a nuisance for a training hall
The optional gymnastics room in the basement offers no spatial qualities
The floor-to-ceiling pivoting windows combined with external sun protection and slats allow only minimal opening and insufficient ventilation
The huge gravelled areas do not offer any quality of stay and restrict use by disabled people
Technical feasibility of the outdoor surface is questionable due to the overhang
Dividing uses into a public ground floor and other uses above prevents a clear address for the department
The spacious staircase only partially compensates for the lack of a central meeting place
Extra-wide corridors and atriums create restrictive constraints
The central zone with lined-up small units results in very long and not particularly attractive routes
The horizontal separation prevents other uses from benefiting spatially from the generous hall volume
The proposed perpendicular parking poses a considerable accident risk due to reversing manoeuvres
Proof of the required number of bicycle parking spaces is not provided
Student areas spread over four storeys impair their functionality
The juxtaposition of laboratory and patient areas creates long distances and unfavourable patient flow
The cafeteria is isolated and remote, only partly suitable as the centre of the department
The hall ancillary rooms need functional revision
Acoustic requirements of the library rooms are not taken into account
This is the largest project in floor area and volume, mainly due to generous circulation
Supporting the two upper floors on only four cores makes the ceiling above the ground floor expensive
Roof dimensions are high because the ground floor is smaller than the basement
Facade costs are expected to be above average
The free play of the ground floor appears a feat of strength not commensurate with the task
The large volumetry, inadequate division of functions, long distances and lack of a central recreational area did not convince
